messages:
izzy: quick flag - the /v1/generate reference still shows `max_tokens` in examples; our runtime uses `max_new_tokens` now and the linter failed on staging. can someone update examples + SDK snippets?

omar: i'll take it. any other mismatch besides the param rename?

izzy: yep - streaming example uses event name `data: delta` in docs, but runtime emits SSE chunks with a `choices` array that has `delta.text`. suggest we show the raw SSE payload and a tiny helper to extract `delta.text`.

claire: good catch. i'll update python/js examples. for python migration note: `input = "\n".join(prompts)` and use `resp.choices[0].delta.get("text", "")` to assemble stream.

sam: also noticed the ruby snippet uses `max_tokens` and constructs `prompt: [..]`. sdk accepts legacy but docs should show canonical `input` string and `max_new_tokens`.

ci-bot: docs linter: docs/generate.md: example-schema-mismatch (line 39) - invalid property `max_tokens`.

omar: opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/834 - replaces `max_tokens` with `max_new_tokens` across examples, converts `prompt` arrays to `input` strings, and updates SSE example to show extraction of `delta.text`. added an examples fixture test.

claire: left wording suggestions to clarify migration: emphasize stable join character and that SDKs tolerate legacy arrays for now. added a one-liner for JS: `const input = prompts.join('\n')`.

sam: pushed a small change to the PR to update the Ruby snippet and fix a stray `max_tokens` in the Go example.

omar: CI checks green on branch. requesting reviews from @claire and @sam.

ci-bot: PR checks: lint ✅, examples schema tests ✅, staging build ✅.

claire: approved and merged. :tada:

izzy: thanks y'all. will add a short changelog bullet and a note in the migration guide so customers see this in release notes.
